faqs.q: How often should I have my heater serviced in Humble?
faqs.a: Once a year, ideally in the fall before the first cold front hits. Humble's mild climate means heaters sit idle for months at a time, which can cause startup issues and wear on components that weren't obvious at the end of last season. An annual tune-up keeps the system clean, calibrated and ready to run when you need it.

faqs.q: What type of heating systems do you service?
faqs.a: We service all major types of residential heating systems: gas furnaces, electric furnaces, heat pumps and dual-fuel systems. We work on all major brands including Carrier, Trane, American Standard and Daikin.

faqs.q: When should I replace my heater instead of repairing it?
faqs.a: A common guideline is the $5,000 rule: multiply the unit's age by the repair cost. If that number exceeds $5,000, replacement usually makes more financial sense. We'll always give you both options with honest recommendations so you can make the right call for your situation.

faqs.q: Are your plumbers licensed in Texas?
faqs.a: Yes. All of our plumbers hold valid Texas plumbing licenses and carry full insurance. Our plumbing license number is RMP44203. Every technician is also background-checked before entering your home.

faqs.q: How much does plumbing repair cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the type and scope of the repair. We always provide an upfront written quote before starting any work so there are no surprises. We also offer financing for larger jobs. Call us for a free estimate.

faqs.q: Do you offer emergency services in all the areas you cover?
faqs.a: Yes. Emergency HVAC, plumbing and electrical services are available across our entire service area. If your AC goes out at midnight or a pipe bursts on a Sunday, we have technicians on call and ready to respond.

faqs.q: Is ductless really more efficient than central AC?
faqs.a: A ductless AC is designed without the main cause of energy loss in central systems: air ducts. That means a mini-split installation in the correct application can dramatically reduce your energy loss.

faqs.q: What is included in an AC tune-up?
faqs.a: An AC tune-up includes cleaning condenser coils, checking refrigerant levels, inspecting electrical connections, clearing condensate drains and making sure the system is cooling at its best. Early spring, March or April, is the best time to book one, before the intense Texas heat arrives.

faqs.q: How long do AC units last in Texas?
faqs.a: Because of the heavy usage here, most AC units in Texas last 10 to 15 years. Regular maintenance is what gets a system to the longer end of that range. A unit under 10 years old with a minor fault is usually worth fixing; one running R-22 refrigerant or needing frequent repairs should be replaced.

faqs.q: Should I repair or replace my water heater?
faqs.a: It depends on the age of the unit and the nature of the problem. If your water heater is under 8 years old and the issue is a failed heating element or thermostat, repair usually makes sense. If it is over 10 years old, or the tank itself is leaking or corroded, replacement is almost always the better call. Our plumbers will give you an honest assessment either way.

faqs.q: Is a tankless water heater worth it in Humble?
faqs.a: For most Humble homeowners, yes, especially if your current tank is aging out and you plan to stay in the home for several years. A tankless unit heats water only when you need it rather than keeping a full tank hot around the clock, and they typically last 20 to 25 years against 10 to 15 for a traditional tank. The upfront cost is higher, so we can run the numbers for your household before you decide.

faqs.q: What counts as an AC emergency?
faqs.a: A total cooling failure during a heatwave, an electrical burning smell, sparking, or water leaking from the indoor unit all need immediate service. Call us rather than waiting, and there is no after-hours fee on HVAC calls at the moment.

faqs.q: How often should I change my air filters?
faqs.a: Every three to six months for most homes. If you have pets, change them more often, every two to four months. It is the simplest thing you can do for both air quality and system efficiency.
